text:
marin: Heads-up — customer C-1842 reporting spikes in latency + unexpected extra charges. They say the SDK appears to be retrying across regions (us-west -> eu-west) instead of staying pinned. Repro/logs below.

marin: logs: ```
[2026-03-10T18:42:01.123Z] request_id=req_01AXYZ region=us-west-2 attempt=1 latency_ms=240
[2026-03-10T18:42:01.371Z] request_id=req_01AXYZ fallback_select=eu-west-1 attempt=2 latency_ms=1800
[2026-03-10T18:42:02.575Z] request_id=req_01AXYZ result=200 route=eu-west-1
``` 
(Notice attempt 2 hit eu-west-1; customer sees cross-region TTLs and 2x billing for same logical request)

josh (infra): Which SDK + config? hedging enabled? backoff params? trace IDs would help. :eyes:

marin: SDK info: redwood-js 2.8.1 (customer). Config snippet they provided:
```js
client = new RedwoodClient({
  hedged: { enabled: true, hedges: 2 },
  timeoutMs: 250,
  backoff: { baseMs: 20, jitter: true },
  regionPreference: 'auto'
})
```
They repro with a synthetic load and see ~3% of requests flip region on retry.

sophie (support): Escalating to billing — customer was billed for tokens served in both regions (ticket B-9921). Are retried requests idempotent? Could be double-charge risk for non-idempotent endpoints. Link: https://redwood.support/tickets/B-9921

avian (eng-runtime): Thanks — likely interplay between hedged/timeout path and our smart routing fallback. Two quick asks:
- can you grab the request trace header (X-Trace-ID) from one of the flipped requests? we need routing decision logs
- can you repro with hedged.enabled=false to confirm reduction in region hops

marin: Trace: X-Trace-ID=trace_0bcd. Attached full routing log (sanitized) — shows route decision at the LB selecting us-west-2 for attempt=1 then fallback policy chose a "closest healthy" which ended up in eu-west-1 because of stale region health metrics.

josh (infra): Reproduced locally with same SDK config. Root cause hypothesis: hedged/parallel attempts use a different routing path that doesn't carry client-affinity metadata (region pin) into the hedged request. So the secondary attempt lands in a different region if local health scores differ. That matches logs.

avian (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations:
- disable hedged retries in SDK (customer-facing): hedged.enabled=false
- increase timeoutMs to 500 so fewer premature hedges
- ops: add routing cookie X-Client-Region or preserve region_hint in hedged fork

sophie (support): Customer approved a temporary config change (disable hedging). We've applied it and they're seeing latency stable. Billing team requests a remediation plan for the double-charge cases.

josh (infra): Proposed remediation: ensure hedged attempt inherits original route headers (region_hint, affinity_id). Add unit tests for hedged path to assert header parity. Also add metric: hedged.region_hop_count to quantify occurrences.

marin: Repro steps I used (minimal):
1) set client hedged: {enabled:true, hedges:2}, timeoutMs:250
2) run 2000 short requests with mix of 20/80 small/large payloads
3) filter traces where latency >1000ms and look for route mismatch
Commands:
```
REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=debug node ./scripts/repro-hedge.js --target customer-c-1842
# then: jq -r '.events[] | select(.route!=.initial_route)'
```

josh (infra): I'll open an infra PR to copy region_hint into hedged forks and also to guard route selection against stale region-health snapshots. Assigning to @avian for runtime changes.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of hedged-headers-fix to infra-canary scheduled at 2026-03-12T02:00:00Z (build id: build-3456) :rocket:

avian (eng-runtime): After infra change we should also ship SDK patch to v2.8.2 that documents hedged behavior and exposes client.pinRegion option. I'll own the SDK release notes and add a migration note for customers.

marin: Thanks — sharing this with C-1842. Closing loop once infra canary passes and SDK 2.8.2 is out. :thumbsup:
